newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec opens territory near Sept-Iles to staking.
newsitem.headline: Quebec opens territory near Sept-Iles to staking.

text.p: Quebec's junior minister of mines, lands and forests, Denise Carrier-Perreault, said on Wednesday that the government removed a prohibition on staking in an 800-square-km area near Sept-Iles.

The lifting of the staking ban, which had been imposed on August 26 after a government geologist discovered promising showings of copper, nickel and cobalt, is expected to spark a staking rush in the area.
The area affected is located about 60 km northeast of Sept-Iles, a port situated 900 km northeast of Montreal along the north shore of the St. Lawrence River.
The minister said about 130 mineral claims covering roughly 20 square km were staked on behalf of the government.
"The government's decision was taken in view of the public interest," Carrier-Perreault said.

She said the government has no intention of developing a mine itself in the area, and added that the discovery will allow important economic benefits for the region, which was under-explored in the past few years.
The government's decision to prohibit staking in the area in August provoked opposition in Quebec's junior mining sector, which clamored for access to claims.
Companies reported to be staking claims in the newly-opened area include St. Genevieve Resources Ltd, and Virginia Gold Mines Inc.
